props.gloss_en: [the Tosefta lists] 'and the karmelit' among the places that are neither private nor public domain
it was needed only for a corner adjacent to the public domain: it is like a karmelit
for though at times the many push and enter it, since its use is inconvenient
between the pillars is judged as a karmelit
though the many tread it, since they cannot pass through it directly, it is like a karmelit
the bench before the pillars is judged as a karmelit
[for the one who said the bench:] it is the bench whose use is inconvenient
but between the pillars, whose use is convenient -- not [a karmelit]
another version: but between the pillars, which the many at times tread, is like the public domain
an upright brick in the public domain: he threw and [the object] stuck to its face -- liable
on top of it -- exempt
Abaye and Rava: provided it is three [handbreadths] high
[at three] the many do not tread on it
but thorns and shrubs -- [on top of them is exempt] even though they are not three high
Chiyya bar Rav: even thorns and shrubs [are not exempt under three]
Chiyya bar Rav: but feces -- not [so: on top of it is exempt]
Rav Ashi: even feces [are not exempt under three]
there is no karmelit less than four [handbreadths]
Rav Sheshet: and it occupies up to ten
proposed: if there is a partition of ten it is a karmelit, and if not, it is not a karmelit
a house not ten high inside, whose roofing completes it to ten: inside it one may carry only four cubits
on its roof one may carry in all of it
rather: up to ten it is a karmelit; above ten handbreadths it is not a karmelit
Shmuel to Rav Yehuda: sharp one, do not busy yourself in Shabbat matters above ten
proposed: [he meant] there is no private domain above ten
Rav Chisda: he stuck a reed in the private domain, threw, and [the object] rested on it -- even a hundred cubits high, he is liable
for the private domain rises to the sky
proposed: [he meant] there is no public domain above ten
one who throws four cubits onto a wall: above ten handbreadths it is like throwing in the air; below ten, like throwing onto the ground
rather: a karmelit -- there is no karmelit above ten
the Sages were lenient with it from the leniencies of the private domain: only if there is a place of four is it a karmelit; if not, it is merely an exempt place
and from the leniencies of the public domain: only up to ten handbreadths is it a karmelit; above ten it is not a karmelit
